selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main goal of this passage at the beginning of the discussion?
questions.answer: It aims to address two major sources of doubt that weaken certainty in faith in the present age.

questions.question: How is the discussion organized for escaping the first danger?
questions.answer: It is organized into two main matters.

questions.question: What example is used to show that a small number of witnesses can outweigh many deniers?
questions.answer: The example is the sighting of the new moon at the start of Ramadan.

questions.question: Why do many denials not add up to a real proof?
questions.answer: Because each denial only reflects a person's own lack of perception, not the actual state of the matter.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens when people affirm a reality on the basis of proof?
questions.answer: Their statements reinforce one another and lead toward agreement.

questions.question: What principle about nonexistence is implied by the example of searching the whole world?
questions.answer: A universal negative claim requires impossible breadth of investigation to prove.

questions.question: Why is it so hard to prove total nonexistence?
questions.answer: Because it would require checking everywhere and every relevant time to rule it out completely.

questions.question: What limited claim may a person properly make from such weakness?
questions.answer: He may say he does not perceive the matter himself.

questions.question: What statement can a denier honestly make about his own limitation?
questions.answer: He can say that he does not see it and therefore does not believe it.

questions.question: What summary contrast is made between affirmation and negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation is unified and mutually supporting; negation is divided and scattered.

questions.question: What issue does this passage focus on instead of repeating earlier detailed proofs?
questions.answer: It focuses on two deep sources of doubt that disturb confidence in faith today.

questions.question: What narrower purpose does this section then take on?
questions.answer: It focuses on two deep pits of doubt that shake confidence in faith in this age.

questions.question: Which religious example is used to make that principle easy to understand?
questions.answer: The beginning-of-Ramadan moon sighting.

questions.question: In that example, why is witness-based affirmation stronger than mass denial?
questions.answer: Because seeing the moon is evidence of its presence, while not seeing it does not show its absence.

questions.question: Why does denial not gather the same strength from numbers?
questions.answer: Because each denier is isolated within his own personal limits and obstacles.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the viewpoint of the person who affirms?
questions.answer: He is directed toward the actual matter itself.

questions.question: If someone wants to prove that something exists, what may be enough?
questions.answer: One clear sign may be enough.

questions.question: What impossible burden falls on someone trying to prove absolute nonexistence?
questions.answer: He must rule out the thing everywhere and across all relevant times.

questions.question: What is the short final principle drawn from the first matter?
questions.answer: Positive proof is unified, while denial breaks apart into many unrelated strands.

questions.question: What is the summary lesson about affirmation and negation?
questions.answer: Affirmation has one shared outcome; negation splits into many disconnected outcomes.

questions.question: Why does the passage say it will not repeat a full explanation of the truth of faith here?
questions.answer: Because that fuller proof has already been established elsewhere, so this section only addresses two major sources of hesitation.

questions.question: How many “Matters” are offered as a way out of the first abyss of doubt?
questions.answer: Two Matters are offered.

questions.question: What role does the Ramadan moon example play in the argument?
questions.answer: It gives a concrete case showing that actual sighting counts more than many people simply failing to see.

questions.question: Why do two ordinary people who actually saw the moon outweigh many scholars who did not?
questions.answer: Because direct witness establishes presence, while failure to notice something does not establish absence.
